args_named.title: Investigation 003: Follow the Constraint - reconstruct the highest-RRT-score congestion episode of May 2026

args_named.statement: The full sequence of publicly observable actions in the episode selected by the pre-declared rule (highest re-trade-cycle score, May 2026) can be reconstructed and its realised cashflows accounted for from public data, with each apparently perverse step explained by the incentives and constraints visible at the time.

args_named.source: elexon-insights May 2026 corpus via evidence/may-manifest.json (companions: neso-may, pn-may, ebocf-may manifests in same evidence dir)

args_named.conclusion: PARTLY CONFIRMED, with the observability boundary precisely mapped. The frozen rule selected constraint group SSE-SP, 2026-05-18..31 (right-censored by the window): 8,259 repeat-curtailment cycles consistent with RRT, 69,869 MWh storage bid-down. The observable sequence reconstructs at scale (excerpt day 2026-05-20: 1,060 cycles; focus unit E_DOLLB-1: 21 cycles, 88 distinct acceptances in one day, repeatedly instructed from scheduled export through zero to around -99 MW import, NONE SO-flagged in the public record). Published money accounts to Elexon's own indicative figures (episode dates, GB-wide scope: storage bids -6,736,338 GBP, storage offers +9,152,108, non-storage offers +78,392,272; SSE-SP published outturn constraint cost 11,510,565 GBP). Two links are NOT publicly observable and are the finding: (1) the intraday re-sale that turns repetition into re-trading; (2) the unit-to-constraint-group mapping that would localise money to the boundary. No figure is a cost of RRT; concurrency is observed, substitution never asserted.

args_named.source: ofgem Repetitive Re-trading (RRT) by electricity storage in transmission constraint periods, policy paper, June 2026; pinned at data/raw/ofgem/repetitive-re-trading-policy-paper-2026-06.pdf via evidence/reference-manifest.json

args_named.conclusion: CORRECTION AND STRENGTHENING of fnd-003-episode-reconstructed (which remains on the record as published). (1) Attribution: the frozen selection rule scores an episode by counting repeat-curtailment cycles across the entire declared GB storage universe over the episode dates; no constraint-group filter was declared and none is publicly implementable - the missing unit-to-group mapping the original finding itself identified. The 8,259 cycles and 69,869 MWh are GB-wide storage activity concurrent with the SSE-SP episode dates and must not be presented as activity behind SSE-SP. (2) Methodology alignment, from the pinned Ofgem RRT policy paper (June 2026, art-003-ofgem-rrt-paper): NESO estimates the balancing cost impact of RRT from storage at approximately GBP 99m in FY 2025/26 (12-hour search window), up from approximately GBP 64m in FY 2024/25, with pumped storage around 80 percent of the two-year total; the methodology counts only settlement periods with a positive FPN, a SYSTEM-FLAGGED bid acceptance, and a subsequent net-upward PN revision within a 3/6/12-hour horizon - computed from timestamped PN revision history that is not public (only final PN vintages are). (3) Descriptive tally over the episode dates (evidence: so-flag-tally.json): 90,020 distinct storage-unit acceptances GB-wide, of which 2,904 (3.2 percent) are SO-flagged; focus unit E_DOLLB-1 recorded 1,492 acceptances with zero SO-flagged, so its 21 excerpt-day cycles cannot be presented as a demonstrated constraint-driven RRT example. Consequence: the repeat-curtailment score is a concurrence signature, not NESO's RRT count, and the public record cannot reproduce NESO's RRT diagnosis - the missing inputs are point-in-time PN revision history and authoritative constraint attribution.
